You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To know if a male dog is fertile, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Research certified veterinary reproductive specialists (2 hours)
Step 2. Schedule a preliminary physical examination (15 minutes)
Step 3. Perform a scrotal ultrasound to check for abnormalities (45 minutes)
Step 4. Review the dog's vaccination and medical history (1 hour)
Step 5. Collect a fresh semen sample via manual stimulation (30 minutes)
Step 6. Conduct a general health checkup including heart and lungs (30 minutes)
Step 7. Purchase specialized microscope slides and coverslips (1 hour)
Step 8. Sanitize the laboratory equipment (20 minutes)
Step 9. Calibrate the sperm motility analysis software (15 minutes)
Step 10. Prepare a warm water bath for sample maintenance (10 minutes)
Step 11. Initial consultation with the veterinarian (30 minutes)
Step 12. Transfer the sample to the laboratory (5 minutes)
Step 13. Centrifuge the sample to concentrate the cells (15 minutes)
Step 14. Check for the presence of Brucellosis in bloodwork (3 days)
Step 15. Apply a specialized stain to the sperm smear (20 minutes)
Step 16. Secure a quiet, distraction-free collection room (30 minutes)
Step 17. Order a comprehensive canine fertility panel (20 minutes)
Step 18. Verify the dog's pedigree and registration papers (1 hour)
Step 19. Draw blood for a baseline testosterone test (15 minutes)
Step 20. Introduce a "teaser" bitch in heat to the environment (1 hour)
Step 21. Pay the laboratory processing fees (10 minutes)
Step 22. Measure the dog's scrotal circumference (5 minutes)
Step 23. Administer a mild stress-reduction supplement (20 minutes)
Step 24. Label the collection vials with the dog's ID (5 minutes)
Step 25. Clean and disinfect the collection area (40 minutes)
Step 26. Pre-warm the collection cone to body temperature (5 minutes)
Step 27. Record the total volume of the ejaculate (5 minutes)
Step 28. Set up the microscope lighting and focus (10 minutes)
Step 29. Evaluate the color and viscosity of the sample (5 minutes)
Step 30. Lay out sterile gloves and lubricant (5 minutes)
Step 31. Prepare the artificial vagina or collection kit (15 minutes)
Step 32. Ensure the room temperature is regulated (30 minutes)
Step 33. Analyze the pH level of the seminal fluid (10 minutes)
Step 34. Check the dog's libido and arousal levels (20 minutes)
Step 35. Verify the bitch's heat cycle stage via swab (2 hours)
Step 36. Evaluate sperm morphology under high magnification (1 hour)
Step 37. Perform a digital rectal exam of the prostate (10 minutes)
Step 38. Prepare the final evaluation report template (15 minutes)
Step 39. Review any previous breeding success records (1 hour)
Step 40. Obtain the owner's written consent for testing (10 minutes)
Step 41. Palpate the testes for size and consistency (10 minutes)
Step 42. Assess the sperm's progressive motility (20 minutes)
Step 43. Count the total number of sperm per milliliter (30 minutes)
Step 44. Observe the dog's gait and orthopedic health (20 minutes)
Step 45. Document any abnormalities in the secondary sperm fraction (15 minutes)
Step 46. Check the dog's identification microchip (5 minutes)
Step 47. Organize the medical files for the specialist (30 minutes)
Step 48. Note any environmental factors like heat stress (15 minutes)
Step 49. Seal the backup sample for cryopreservation (10 minutes)
Step 50. Final review of all diagnostic findings by the vet (1 hour)
